t:
(a) Redesignation.—The first section of the Act of March 3, 1931 (46 Stat. 1509, chapter 439; 16 U.S.C. 674a), is amended by striking “Sullys Hill National Game Preserve” and inserting “White Horse Hill National Game Preserve”. 
    (b) Conforming Amendment.—Section 2 of the Act of March 3, 1931 (46 Stat. 1509, chapter 439; 16 U.S.C. 674b), is amended by striking “Sullys Hill National Game Preserve” and inserting “White Horse Hill National Game Preserve”. 
    (c) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the Sullys Hill National Game Preserve shall be considered to be a reference to the “White Horse Hill National Game Preserve”.

fable.w: This section only renames a game preserve and makes conforming amendments and a references clause. The mention of a "regulation" in subsection (c) might tempt a Yes, but it merely deems existing references to use the new name; it does not authorize rulemaking or involve any outside party in a federal decision. No consultation, hearing, advisory body, comment period, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: is amended by striking “Sullys Hill National Game Preserve” and inserting “White Horse Hill National Game Preserve”

opus.w: The section only renames a national game preserve and updates references to the old name. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue, and no one outside the federal government takes part in any decision. The word "regulation" names a kind of existing record; it does not grant power to make new rules, so it does not count as rulemaking.
opus.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the Sullys Hill National Game Preserve shall be considered to be a reference to the “White Horse Hill National Game Preserve”.
opus.b: I'm labelling this "No". The tempting wrong reading is that the word "regulation" in subsection (c) suggests rulemaking. It doesn't: it only lists regulations among the existing records whose references to the old name are updated. It does not authorize any new rule.

qwen_chat.w: This section solely amends the name of a national game preserve from 'Sullys Hill' to 'White Horse Hill' and updates references accordingly. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. The text is a straightforward legislative renaming provision with no procedural requirements for external input.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that renaming a preserve involves public input or consultation, but the text itself contains no such requirement. It is purely a legislative amendment changing a name.
